labels.label: rem:mesure_unilaterale
labels.notes: Lean >= paper in the readings DEC-25, OQ-18, OQ-34/OQ-35, OQ-82, and the row is rightly partial. mesure_unilaterale (l.306) asks [T2Space M], any [MeasurableSpace M], C absolutely minimal with IsoChartsCoverDEC25 over massAModelCausality, and sing_0(M) nonempty. It concludes that no measure is admissible both ways. Against ETT.tex:1716-1723: 'causal' is dropped, since isCausal_of_admissiblePast derives it from the measure. Second countability is dropped. 'p<q two BTZ points of one line' becomes sing_0 nonempty, the pair being produced by exists_le_ne_of_mem_sing through SFALine.line. Every sigma-algebra is covered, Borel among them. The natural causality is covered by mesure_unilaterale_of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25. mesure_unilaterale_sharp adds strong causality, second countability and Borel only for the existence half (prop:mesure_admissible), which is correct. epi_admissible_both is a sound use of E_pi: it satisfies hmin and hC (SFALocal.nonvacuous_epi), has sing_0 empty, and carries one measure admissible both ways. Non-vacuity is checked: nonvacuous_e0_unilaterale reaches the hypotheses and the conclusion through mesure_unilaterale_sharp. Cited unmarked at positions 361, 2207 and 3318.

labels.notes: This label is a disclosed special case, and the row is partial. The printed claim ('a spacetime') is false in general (the lightlike line, the existing finding), so a form at E>=0-manifolds is the strongest true one. not_admissible_both_of_chain (l.198) keeps the strict obstruction's chain reading (WP-3): p <= q, p != q, J^-(q)\J^-(p) inside J^+(p), and empty I^- along it. It discharges K^+(p) inside I^+(p) through Kplus_eq_Iplus, which is SFABTZ.K_calcul (a) off sing_0 and (b) on it. I checked the cases against SFABTZ.lean:656-660. It assumes no T2, no countability and no causality. Iminus_eq_empty_iff and chain_subset_sing are correct. Note that chain_subset_sing proves only that the set lies in sing_0(M); a segment needs T2 and causality (Jminus_diff_eq_segment). nonvacuous_e0_chain exposes every hypothesis of Causality.not_admissiblePast_and_admissibleFuture_of_pushUp at E_0, including [FirstCountableTopology]. Its last two conjuncts are the same proposition, proved by two routes (cosmetic). The docstring checklist row for this label does not flag 'a spacetime' -> E>=0-manifold as strengthened; the REPORT does.

labels.notes: geroch_sing_i_imp_ii and geroch_sing_i_imp_iii (l.382, l.393) ask [T2Space M], [SecondCountableTopology M], hmin, hC and hG only. Connectedness and strong causality are dropped, and strong causality is rederived from global hyperbolicity through tarentin (GloballyHyperbolic.stronglyCausal, SFALocal.tarentin). No MeasurableSpace or ModelMeasures is left: Borel is installed inside the proof, and massA_modelMeasures and SFAManifolds.singularFlatAxioms are applied. The conclusion of (i)=>(ii) is a Cauchy time function plus strict increase, which is stronger (DEC-15). geroch_sing_ii_imp_iii (l.403) asks strong causality (DEC-18) and no connectedness. geroch_sing_split (l.416) asks connectedness, causality (weaker than DEC-18's strong causality) and the named VecteurFlow (kb/0022, disclosed, 'strengthened'). The equivalence (geroch_sing, geroch_sing_of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25) asks connected, T2, second countable and strongly causal E>=0-manifolds, which is the paper's reading. It rests on the disclosed tagged sorry geroch_sing_iii_imp_i, and the row stays partial with lean_stated scaffold. Witnesses come out of the M-level theorems: E_0 (nonvacuous_e0_geroch carries every hypothesis of geroch_sing; nonvacuous_e0_natural) and E_pi (nonvacuous_epi_geroch). Cited unmarked at positions 451, 1030 and 2542.

findings.what: The finding is true and new. It holds only in the library's reading of defi:mesure_dieckmann property 3, where p<q means p <= q and p != q (AdmissiblePast.pos). The paper's own use at ETT.tex:1275 supports that reading ('property 3 applied to any q in J^+(p)\{p}'). Under a strict-preorder reading (p <= q and not q <= p) the finding would fail. The wording does not say which reading it uses. On defi:mesure_dieckmann (l.1034-1043) it is a consequence, not an error: only causal spacetimes carry an admissible measure in either sense. It also shows that the causality hypothesis of prop:mesure_dieckmann_topo and of SingularFlatAxioms.mesure_admissible is necessary for their conclusions. It generalises the sub-claim of the DEC-18 finding (rem:singular_flat_spacetime_therefore) that E_alpha modulo a translation carries no measure admissible in the past.

findings.what: I checked the argument by hand and it is correct. ChartIso (Causal/GXStructure.lean:82) asks, for every open U inside the chart source, C.le U x y <-> D.le (chartImage e U) (e x) (e y), and the same for lt. Every non-empty open set of a model (minkowski 2, E_0, E_kappa) contains a short null pair x <= y, x != y, with not x << y: take a small flat convex ball off the singular line, where <<_W is contained in <<. chronoMinkowski = (minkowski n).reflChrono has <=_U given by x = y or x <<_U y, so it admits no such pair, and IsoChartsCoverDEC25 fails at every point for every singular structure. So OQ-33's witness does not reach geroch_sing. The finding is a refinement of the theo:geroch_sing row's second paper_finding and of OQ-33's own text ('the paper's theorem is not refuted, since genuine singular flat spacetimes have the models' locally closed relations'). It concerns the formalization, not the paper. 'So the paper's theorem, read at E>=0-manifolds, is not refuted' should say only that this witness does not refute it: the statement is neither proved nor refuted there. The SORRY tag (l.561) has kb 0006's form and states the obstruction precisely enough. Its 'the library has neither' is right if it is read as quasi-limits plus the J^-(q) cap J^+(S) compactness. lem:densite_modele itself is proved in the models (ModelRowsE0.densite_modele, minkowski_densite, massive_densite), so a sharper tag would say so.

(lem:densite_modele, proved in the models, not transported to M; OQ-33) ... the library has neither the quasi-limits nor that compactness'.

rem:mesure_unilaterale.notes_append: T-ett-singular-rows-geroch (atlas-team, 2026-11-21), audit AUDIT-1 minor (fixed at graduation), Causal/Remarks/SingularRowsGeroch.lean: the remark at M itself, not under SingularFlatAxioms. At every Hausdorff E≥0-manifold with a BTZ point, no measure is admissible in the past and in the future at once. This holds for every absolutely minimal causality with an isomorphic chart at each point, the natural one included, mixed manifolds included (mesure_unilaterale, mesure_unilaterale_of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25). Neither causality nor second countability is assumed. The paper's computation at M: J⁻(q) ∖ J⁻(p) is the segment γ(]t₀, 0]) of the BTZ line through q (Jminus_diff_eq_segment, M causal). It lies in (J⁺(p) ∖ K⁺(p)) ∩ sing₀(M) since K⁺(p) = I⁺(p) (segment_subset), and properties 3. and 4. conflict there (not_admissible_both_of_le). The remark is sharp at strongly causal, second countable E≥0-manifolds (mesure_unilaterale_sharp, through SFAManifolds.mesure_admissible). The BTZ point is needed: E_π carries a measure admissible both ways (epi_admissible_both). Witnesses come out of the M-level theorems: E₀ (nonvacuous_e0_unilaterale, nonvacuous_e0_natural). Hypotheses: E≥0-manifold → read (DEC-25, OQ-18); causal → weakened (isCausal_of_admissiblePast); Hausdorff → carried; second countable → weakened; p < q two BTZ points of one line → weakened (q BTZ, p ≤ q, p ≠ q; or sing₀(M) ≠ ∅); a measure → carried (any σ-algebra); E₀ and Isom(E^{1,2}) → read (OQ-34, OQ-35; OQ-82). The strict SingularFlatAxioms forms above remain the abstract route.
rem:mesure_unilaterale.paper_findings_add: ETT.tex:1716, « Let M be a causal E≥0-manifold »: the conclusion does not need « causal ». Read property 3 of defi:mesure_dieckmann with p < q meaning p ≤ q and p ≠ q, as the paper uses it at l.1275. Then a causality carrying a measure admissible in the past, or in the future, is causal: for x ≤ y ≤ x with x ≠ y the set J⁻(y) ∖ J⁻(x) is empty, so property 3 fails (Causal.SingularRowsGeroch.isCausal_of_admissiblePast, isCausal_of_admissibleFuture; model-free). Hence the remark holds at every Hausdorff E≥0-manifold with a BTZ point (mesure_unilaterale). The computation uses causality for the segment ]p, q], so the word may stay. The totally vicious example behind DEC-18 (rem:singular_flat_spacetime_therefore) is an instance.

defi:mesure_dieckmann.notes_append: Model-free consequence, not a finding: any causality carrying a measure admissible in the past or in the future is causal (Causal.SingularRowsGeroch.isCausal_of_admissiblePast, isCausal_of_admissibleFuture; p < q read as p ≤ q, p ≠ q, as at l.1275). So causality is necessary for the conclusions of prop:mesure_dieckmann_topo and prop:mesure_admissible. T-ett-singular-rows-geroch.

At every E≥0-manifold (C absolutely minimal with an isomorphic chart at each point; no Hausdorff, countability or causality hypothesis) the obstruction holds with K⁺(p) ⊆ I⁺(p) discharged. K⁺(p) = I⁺(p) at every point (Kplus_eq_Iplus, SFABTZ.K_calcul (a), (b)), hence not_admissible_both_of_chain. There I⁻(r) = ∅ iff r ∈ sing₀(M) (Iminus_eq_empty_iff), so such a chain lies in sing₀(M) (chain_subset_sing). The hypotheses of the _of_pushUp form hold at every BTZ segment of a causal Hausdorff E≥0-manifold (pushUp_obstruction_hypotheses, exists_pushUp_obstruction). They are exhibited at E₀ (nonvacuous_e0_chain); before, they were met only inside the proof of E0.mesure_unilaterale. Hypotheses: « a spacetime » → strengthened (an E≥0-manifold; false in general); the chain → carried (WP-3's reading); K⁺(p) ⊆ I⁺(p) → discharged; Hausdorff, second countable, causal → weakened (not assumed); E₀ and Isom(E^{1,2}) → read (OQ-34, OQ-35; OQ-82). The sentence above « what is missing is SingularFlatAxioms for every E≥0-manifold » has been stale since T-ett-singular-sfa (SFAManifolds.singularFlatAxioms); the M-level form does not need it.

So at E≥0-manifolds the remark holds as printed, with no Hausdorff, countability or causality hypothesis (not_admissible_both_of_chain); such a chain lies in sing₀(M) (chain_subset_sing). »

theo:geroch_sing.notes_append: T-ett-singular-rows-geroch (atlas-team, 2026-11-21), audit AUDIT-1 minor (fixed at graduation), Causal/Remarks/SingularRowsGeroch.lean; the equivalence is in the scaffold remainder CausalScaffold.SingularRowsGeroch. The results are stated at M itself, for every absolutely minimal causality with an isomorphic chart at each point, the natural one included. (i)⇒(ii) and (i)⇒(iii) hold at every Hausdorff, second countable E≥0-manifold with no hypothesis left (geroch_sing_i_imp_ii, geroch_sing_i_imp_iii and their _of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25 forms). There SingularFlatAxioms comes from SFAManifolds.singularFlatAxioms, ModelMeasures from MeasuresManifolds.massA_modelMeasures, and strong causality from global hyperbolicity (stronglyCausal_of_globallyHyperbolic). Connectedness and strong causality are not used in these two directions. (ii)⇒(iii) holds at every strongly causal one (geroch_sing_ii_imp_iii). The splitting holds at every connected causal one given VecteurFlow (geroch_sing_split). The equivalence at connected, strongly causal E≥0-manifolds is stated (CausalScaffold.SingularRowsGeroch.geroch_sing, geroch_sing_of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25) and rests only on geroch_sing_iii_imp_i (OQ-32). OQ-33's witness, chronological Minkowski space, does not satisfy its hypotheses: it has an isomorphic chart at no point (by hand, not formalized). VecteurFlow has no witness at E₀. At a BTZ point the orbit of lem:vecteur's X is null (l.1756), so the chronal-flow splitting (HasChronalCausalFlow.nonempty_isCauchySplitting) does not apply there; only IsCausalFlow.exists_isCauchySplitting could, given J^±(S) closed. Witnesses: E₀ (nonvacuous_e0_geroch, nonvacuous_e0_natural) and E_π (nonvacuous_epi_geroch). Hypotheses: singular flat spacetime → read (DEC-25, OQ-18); connected → carried by the equivalence and the splitting, weakened elsewhere; strongly causal → carried (DEC-18) by (ii)⇒(iii) and the equivalence, weakened in (i)⇒(ii) and (i)⇒(iii); the measures → discharged; (ii) → read (DEC-15); (iii) → read (DEC-14); « homeomorphic to Σ × ℝ » → strengthened (VecteurFlow); E₀ and Isom(E^{1,2}) → read (OQ-34, OQ-35; OQ-82).
paper_findings_edit: Second finding, append: « Stated at genuine E≥0-manifolds (IsoChartsCoverDEC25; CausalScaffold.SingularRowsGeroch.geroch_sing), the theorem is out of this witness's reach. Not formalized. »
